title: Pre-agreed KPIs let deposit caps and yield expansions move without a formal Artifact edit
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.2.1.3.3 lists among the Capital & Operational Plan's required elements "Performance-based Adjustments: define the conditions or KPIs that allow adjustments to Instance deposit caps or yield expansions without requiring a formal Artifact edit."

This is meta-governance. Every other route to changing an Instance runs through the process in A.2.2.10.1.1.2.2 — drafting an Artifact update, Operational Executor Facilitator review, an off-chain snapshot vote, then publication. Performance-based Adjustments move the decision earlier: governance approves a *rule* for changing parameters once, and subsequent changes execute against it without a vote.

The motivation is that scaling a working Instance is a decision whose criteria are knowable in advance, and forcing each increment through a full vote makes governance the bottleneck on capital efficiency while producing little new information.

The trade-off is that the ecosystem now commits to the calibration of the trigger rather than to the outcomes it produces. A KPI that correlates with yield but not with risk will keep authorising expansion through exactly the conditions where a human reviewer would stop. Because approval is granted at plan time, the review burden shifts entirely onto the specificity of the KPIs — the same C&O Plan section also demands a Data Submission Protocol and Emergency Procedures, which is what makes an automatic expansion path defensible.
description: The C&O Plan defines conditions under which Instance parameters adjust automatically, converting repeated governance votes into a rule approved once
